body:
### Problem

Basically with the new setting of `scrolloffpad=1` and `scrolloff=999` the last line of the buffer gets centered when reaching it with j but it doesn't get centered with `<C-d>` as if half-page-down could not place the cursor in the last line properly.

### Steps to reproduce

nvim --clean
(open long file)
:set scrolloff=999
:set scrolloffpad=1
(press `<C-d>` until reaching bottom of buffer you will see it doesn't get to the very last line or gets centered, if you press j until buffer bottom instead it does.)

### Expected behavior

pressing `<C-d>` should also let the cursor get to the last line and center the last line vertically with scrolloffpad=1

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1357+g53211ade2b

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

idk

### Operating system/version

NixOS 26.11 (Zokor) x86_64

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.48.2

### $TERM environment variable

tmux-256color

### Installation

bob

comment_data.body: Did this only start recent recently? since you mentioned "nightly"
true, I wouldn't say recently. I'm just aware that scrolloffpad is in nightly.

tested with NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1364+g9bd18d04f1 and a ~8000 loc file.
:set scrolloff=999
:set scrolloffpad=1
`<C-d>` scrolling stops at the middle of the window. -> works as expected.

```vim
	When 'scrolloff' and 'scrolloffpad' are greater than zero, allow
	the cursor to remain centered when at the end of the file.
	Normally, 'scrolloff' will not keep the cursor centered at the
	end of the file.

```
I can record a video to showcase better what I mean maybe. allow me some time

No video necessary - the behavior with this options is exactly as described in the docs:
```vim
:help 'scrolloffpad'
```
I think this issue could be closed.

yes I understood after the edit. although I still don't get why not let the cursor reach the very EOF with `<C-d>` with scrolloffpad=1? Because with only scrolloff=999 the cursor can reach EOF no problem with `<C-d>`
in fact when the cursor is at the last line with both scrolloff & scrolloffpad and you press `<C-d>` the cursor is taken upwards, that makes no sense IMO

Try something like
vim.opt.scroll         = 10
vim.opt.scrolloff      = 2
and leave scrolloffpad=0 unchanged. This scrolls to the last line.

yea but that doesn't preserve scrolloff=999 which the setting I use and of course I want to start using scrolloffpad=1 too, I like both things it's only that I wonder why such weird behaviour with `<C-d>` not being able to reach last line under that combination

also it's true that it behaves differently with something like scrolloff=10. because it let's `<C-d>` with scrolloffpad=1 reach last line but then it doesn't center the buffer as scrolloffpad=1 is intended for. and if you go one line up after reaching last line with `<C-d>` the buffer does get centered, basically jumping

Hm what you want to archieve: 
1) Always keep the cursorline in the middle of the window
2) On EOF allow to scroll to the end

The example with 999 in the docs is poorly chosen.

You can set your goal with a autocmd. This should be better.
```lua
local function set_scrolloff()
  vim.opt.scrolloff = math.floor(vim.api.nvim_win_get_height(0) / 2)
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("WinResized", {
  callback = set_scrolloff,
})

set_scrolloff()
```

@justinmk Is there a better way to handle this?

Ok this could potentialy a bug:
:set scrolloff=999
:set scrolloffpad=1
When cursor is on the last line of the buffer (moved manually), `<C-d>` performs an upward scroll like `<C-u>` with the corresponding `vim.opt.scroll`
A better behavior in this case would be that `<C-d` does nothing.

> [@justinmk](https://github.com/justinmk) Is there a better way to handle this?

not sure, i don't understand 'scrolloffpad'. the docs make no sense, and when i tried it, i didn't see any useful behavior.

exactlyy. well of course not that I am entitled but I propose that `<C-d>` get handled just like `j` but it simply does the usual half page jumps. In the sense that it is allowed to reach the last line instead of getting stuck at the middle of the screen before getting to the bottom of the buffer, and allowing it to center the buffer with scrolloffpad=1 just like `j` does

> exactlyy. well of course not that I am entitled but I propose that `<C-d>` get handled just like `j` 

I'm not entitled either.. but this is a bad suggestion. Scrolling should always be scrolling.
If you set `vim.opt.scroll` and `vim.opt.scrolloff` - the behavior is fine. (scrolls and also scrolls to the end of the file) Just avoid the `scrolloffpad`

If somebody wants the cursorline always to be kept at the middle of the window - a autocmd is necessary or maybe a new introduced option? I think this use case is very rare..

Avoid `scrolloffpad` this causes problems described in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41383#issuecomment-5346451302
The purpose and the behavior of this option needs to be clarified by the core team. I don't see any use case for this.

> Scrolling should always be scrolling.

I didn't mean the opposite of this. 

It's ok I understand that this a rare usecase but I mean scrolloffpad was (as far as I know) recently introduced in nightly as it isn't in 0.12.4 so why not polish it further and come to terms with what it currently does. I am willing to take a shot and draft a PR and explain better my proposal

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39248

I will open an issue for vim about the `<C-d>` does `<C-u>` on the last line
https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/21096

ok I have fixed it locally. maybe this is not the best recording but I think it works.

- first part from start to 0:20 is unfixed current nightly neovim
- second part is my local neovim of course with the fix

please let me know if you want to see another recording and/or if the behavior is reasonable

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cee702ef-6b34-4904-a441-ce508856149d

I did with the help of AI but I don't want to provide some slop so if you guys agree with the behaviour I will refine it further as it isn't a lot of lines and prepare it according to the repo standards. I'd like to do this right
